sections.title: OS Fundamentals & Architecture
sections.hindiTitle: ऑपरेटिंग सिस्टम की बुनियादी बातें एवं संरचना
sections.overview: An Operating System (OS) is system software that acts as an intermediary between computer hardware and the user. It manages system resources, executes programs, and provides a stable, consistent environment.
sections.hindiOverview: ऑपरेटिंग सिस्टम (OS) सिस्टम सॉफ्टवेयर है जो कंप्यूटर हार्डवेयर और उपयोगकर्ता के बीच मध्यस्थ के रूप में कार्य करता है। यह सिस्टम संसाधनों का प्रबंधन करता है।

keyFunctions.name: Processor Management
keyFunctions.desc: Process scheduling, context switching, CPU allocation algorithms (FCFS, SJF, Round Robin, Priority).

keyFunctions.name: Memory Management
keyFunctions.desc: Tracks primary memory allocation, paging, segmentation, virtual memory, and swapping.

keyFunctions.name: File Management
keyFunctions.desc: Organizes directory structures, file allocation tables (FAT/NTFS), permissions, and file access control.

keyFunctions.name: Device Management
keyFunctions.desc: Communicates with hardware devices using dedicated Device Drivers and I/O controllers (buffering, caching, spooling).

keyFunctions.name: Security & Protection
keyFunctions.desc: User authentication, access control lists (ACL), process isolation, firewall coordination.

keyFunctions.name: User Interface
keyFunctions.desc: Provides CLI (Command Line Interface - e.g., Bash, CMD) and GUI (Graphical User Interface - e.g., Windows Explorer, macOS Aqua).

spoolingVsBuffering.spooling: Simultaneous Peripheral Operations On-Line (SPOOLing) overlaps I/O of one job with computation of other jobs. Uses disk as a very large buffer (e.g., Print Spooler).
spoolingVsBuffering.buffering: Temporarily stores data in main memory (RAM) while being transferred between devices or application to compensate for speed mismatch.

examTips: SPOOLing uses hard disk as buffer, while Buffering uses main memory (RAM). High-frequency bank exam question!
Virtual Memory uses secondary storage (Hard disk/SSD) to simulate additional RAM when physical RAM is insufficient.
Thrashing occurs when the system spends more time paging (swapping pages between RAM and disk) than executing actual instructions.

types.desc: Jobs with similar needs are batched together and executed without user interaction. No direct interaction between user and computer during execution.
Multiple programs reside in main memory simultaneously. CPU switches between jobs to keep CPU utilization high.
CPU executes multiple tasks concurrently by rapidly switching between them (Time quantum/slice). Each user gets a share of CPU time.
Guarantees strict deadlines for task completion. Hard RTOS has zero tolerance for missing deadlines (missed deadline = catastrophe). Soft RTOS tolerates minor delays with degraded quality.
types.example: VxWorks, QNX, RTLinux (Used in missile guidance, ATMs, medical monitors).

types.desc: Manages a collection of independent networked computers, presenting them to the user as a single coherent system.
Runs on a dedicated server and manages network traffic, shared printers, files, and security.
types.example: Windows Server, Novell NetWare, Red Hat Enterprise Linux.

types.desc: Designed for compact devices with limited power and resources.
types.example: Android (based on Linux kernel), iOS, iPadOS, Tizen.

sections.title: File Systems & Storage Management

comparison.name: FAT16
comparison.features: Legacy MS-DOS, 16-bit cluster addresses, no file permissions.

comparison.name: FAT32
comparison.features: Supported everywhere (USB drives), no security permissions, no journaling.

comparison.name: NTFS
comparison.features: Windows default since XP. Journaling, file compression, EFS encryption, granular permissions (ACL), disk quotas.

comparison.name: exFAT
comparison.features: Optimized for flash memory (SD cards, USBs) without FAT32's 4GB file limit, cross-platform with Mac.

comparison.name: ext4
comparison.features: Standard Linux file system. Journaling, backwards compatibility with ext2/ext3.

comparison.name: APFS / HFS+
comparison.features: Apple File System (APFS) optimized for SSDs, snapshots, crash protection.

examTraps: Question: What is the maximum file size supported by FAT32? Answer: 4 GB (specifically 4GB minus 1 byte).
Question: Which file system introduced file encryption and journaling in Windows? Answer: NTFS (New Technology File System).

steps.name: Power On
steps.detail: Power supply sends Power Good signal to the motherboard clock generator.

steps.name: CPU Reset
steps.detail: CPU executes jump instruction at standard memory address (0xFFFF0 in x86) pointing to ROM BIOS.

steps.name: POST (Power-On Self-Test)
steps.detail: Firmware checks hardware integrity (RAM, keyboard, video card, disk). Beep codes signal errors if screen is inactive.

steps.name: Boot Device Selection
steps.detail: Firmware searches configured boot order (SSD, HDD, USB, Network) for boot sector.

steps.name: MBR / GPT & Bootloader
steps.detail: Loads Master Boot Record (MBR - Sector 0) or GUID Partition Table (GPT) and hands control to Windows Boot Manager (BOOTMGR) or GRUB.

steps.name: Kernel Initialization
steps.detail: OS Kernel is loaded into RAM (ntoskrnl.exe in Windows, vmlinuz in Linux), loads critical drivers.

steps.name: User Space & Shell
steps.detail: System processes launch, login screen displays, user shell initializes.

typesOfBooting.coldBoot: Hard Boot - Starting the computer from a completely powered-off state by pressing the power button.
typesOfBooting.warmBoot: Soft Boot - Restarting the computer while it is already running (via OS restart command or Ctrl+Alt+Del) without cutting main electrical power.

biosVsUefi.bios: Basic Input/Output System: Legacy 16-bit mode, MBR partition table (max 2TB disks, 4 primary partitions), slow boot.
biosVsUefi.uefi: Unified Extensible Firmware Interface: Modern 32/64-bit, GPT partition table (up to 9.4 ZB, 128 partitions), Secure Boot feature, graphical mouse interface.

sections.title: Linux & Unix Essentials for Bank Exams
sections.hindiTitle: बैंक परीक्षाओं हेतु लिनक्स और यूनिक्स आवश्यक कमांड
sections.overview: Linux is an open-source Unix-like kernel released in 1991 by Linus Torvalds. Unix was created at Bell Labs in 1969 by Ken Thompson and Dennis Ritchie.

topCommands.desc: List directory contents (`ls -l` for long format with permissions).
Print Working Directory (shows current absolute path).
Change directory (`cd ..` goes up one level, `cd ~` goes to home).
Remove files or directories (`rm -r` for recursive removal).
Copy files or directories (`cp file1 file2`).
Move or rename files (`mv old new`).
Concatenate and display file content on terminal.
Global Regular Expression Print - searches text for matching patterns.
Change file access permissions (e.g. `chmod 755 script.sh` - Read=4, Write=2, Execute=1).
Terminate a process by its PID (Process ID) (`kill -9 PID` sends SIGKILL).
Display reference manual pages for any command.
